title: Where Will the International Space Station Crash?
description:
Where Will the International Space Station Crash?

NASA plans to operate the International Space Station—which spans 109 metres end to end, like an American football field—through 2030 (with a 2027 assessment on whether to launch the U.S. Deorbit Vehicle in 2029 or extend operations). Under the baseline plan, most hardware will vaporise on re-entry while the deorbit craft performs its final burn at the end of 2030 or early 2031 to steer the rest into an uninhabited region of the South Pacific Ocean.

Sources: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-107805 (2027 decision point; mid-2029 USDV launch; end-2030 or early-2031 re-entry burn that pushes the station into a remote part of the ocean), NASA ISS Transition Report, Jan 2022 (target: the South Pacific Oceanic Uninhabited Area, around Point Nemo) & NASA International Space Station Facts and Transition Plan FAQ (109 m / 356 ft end-to-end, American football field; operates through 2030; orbits over 90% of Earth's population).
